expected: Pricing states what "1x" means: the baseline plan behind 5x/15x and its concrete allowance.

section: Free / Basic / Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x planning structure
feature: Explicit identification of the allowance being multiplied.
expected: Plan copy names exactly which allowance a multiplier scales (e.g. managed-usage credits per 5-hour, weekly and monthly window).

section: Free / Basic / Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x planning structure
expected: Plans differ in feature access (not just usage), the differences are listed, and each gate is enforced server-side.

section: Free / Basic / Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x planning structure
expected: Plans differ in generation settings (e.g. reasoning effort, manual model choice), the UI shows the gated options, and the server clamps requests to the plan.

section: Free / Basic / Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x planning structure
expected: Plans carry caps specific to a model class (flagship models get their own weekly cap), shown to users and enforced on admission.

section: Free / Basic / Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x planning structure
expected: When a renewal payment fails, the plan follows a defined grace rule and the user is told what access remains and how to fix it.

section: Free / Basic / Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x planning structure
expected: One account plan applies on every signed-in surface: each surface reads the same server-side entitlement and the server enforces it per surface.

section: Free / Basic / Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x planning structure
expected: Each plan explains its own features (what it adds over the current plan, and why a blocked feature needs a given plan).
Every signed-in surface shows the account's current plan, read from the server.
Users can see the current billing period: when it renews or ends.
An overall usage meter shows how much of the plan allowance is used.
Users can see usage broken down by model (at least the flagship-model cap and per-model spend).
Users can see how much of their usage went to coding and agentic work.
Users can see how many credits remain (plan windows and purchased balance).
Users can tell purchased credits apart from the plan's included allowance.
Each usage window shows how long until it resets.
Users can see usage per task (agent run / work session).
After a task finishes, the user sees what it actually cost.
Users are warned before they hit a usage limit.
When a limit is reached the user sees a clear blocked state explaining which limit and what they can do.
When a limit or plan blocks the chosen model, the user is offered an eligible alternative model.
At a limit, the user is offered waiting until the reset, with the reset time, as an alternative to paying.
When a payment fails, the user is told clearly (checkout or renewal) and shown how to fix it.
A scheduled (end-of-period) cancellation is shown with its date.
The user can set a default model that new conversations start with.
The user can set a default reasoning effort used for new turns.
The user can choose the default mode new conversations start in (e.g. chat vs agent/work, ask vs auto).
Settings let the user view and customise (disable or rebind) keyboard shortcuts.
The user can view and edit their account profile (name, photo, email) on the surface, and the change is saved to the account.
The user can write custom instructions on the surface and they are applied to that surface's chats until changed or switched off.
The user can see, add, edit and delete saved memories on the surface and turn memory on or off, and saved memories are used in that surface's chats.
The user can choose whether crash reports and diagnostics are sent, and the choice is honoured.
The user can list archived chats, restore them, and delete them.
The user can see devices paired for remote use (phone to desktop, browser to desktop) and unpair them.
The user can sign out of the current device or app.
The user can review the approvals they chose to remember (always-allow/deny) and remove any of them.
The user can set the default approval posture for agent actions (ask every time, auto-approve safe, autonomous) and it is enforced.
The user can turn on a hardened mode that tightens account and agent security beyond defaults.
Screens that need explaining link straight to the matching help or docs article for that feature.
A user can report a bug from the product, with enough context (build, platform) for support to act.
Users can send general product feedback from inside the product and it is stored for the team.
Users can submit a feature request from inside the product and it is stored for the team.
A user can produce a diagnostic bundle, see what it contains, and choose to share it with support.
When a request fails, the user sees a reference id they can quote to support.
A desktop companion pairs with the user's phone so desktop work can be started, watched or approved from the phone.
The app shows whether the local model runtime is running and healthy, with errors when it is not.
